title: Learning from generic language.
title_zh: 从通用语言中学习（Learning from generic language）
abstract: Generic language (e.g., "Birds have hollow bones") conveys generalizations about categories and is a fundamental and ubiquitous mechanism of learning about the world. How exactly learning from generics occurs, however, is unclear: Generics exhibit so much flexibility in how they are interpreted that a formal, quantitative theory of how generic language updates beliefs has not only never been developed or tested, but the very notion has often been explicitly dismissed. Here, we explore a hypothesis implicit in the work of Tessler and Goodman (2019) that generics update beliefs via an uncertain threshold, like a vague quantifier: A category-property generic ("Ks F") means that the property F is expected to be relatively widespread in the category K, where the threshold for being relatively widespread is a priori uncertain and resolved by consulting one's prior knowledge of the property. We compare this model to a family of alternatives with the same background knowledge but where generics have a fixed, context-invariant threshold meaning. We additionally formalize a novel quantitative model of an explicitly conceptual-based approach to generics, which does not involve any thresholds, where generics would act as a direct connection to conceptual structures. Across three experiments in which we both measure and manipulate prior beliefs, we find the uncertain threshold approach to generics to be the best explanation of participants' highly context-sensitive interpretations of novel generic statements. The sufficiency of this rational model of generic interpretation suggests that generics are an effective medium for faithful transmission of knowledge between interlocutors, arguing against proposals that generic language interpretation is biased in a fundamental way. This work adds to the growing enterprise of formal, quantitative studies of human understanding of generic language. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).
abstract_zh: 通用语言（例如“鸟类有空心骨”）传达关于类别的一般化信息，是学习世界的基本且普遍机制。然而，通用语言如何学习的具体机制尚不清楚：通用语言在解释上具有极大灵活性，以至于关于通用语言如何更新信念的正式定量理论既未被开发也未被检验，甚至这一概念常被明确否定。本文探讨了Tessler和Goodman（2019）工作中隐含的假设，即通用语言通过不确定阈值（类似模糊量词）来更新信念：类别-属性通用语（“Ks F”）意味着属性F在类别K中相对普遍，而“相对普遍”的阈值先验不确定，并通过参考对该属性的先验知识来确定。我们将此模型与一组具有相同背景知识但通用语具有固定、与上下文无关阈值含义的替代模型进行比较。我们还正式化了一种新颖的定量模型，基于显式概念化的方法，不涉及任何阈值，通用语在此模型中直接与概念结构相连。通过三项实验，我们既测量又操纵先验信念，发现不确定阈值方法最能解释参与者对新颖通用语句的高度上下文敏感解释。该理性模型的充分性表明，通用语言是传递知识的有效媒介，反驳了通用语言解释在根本上存在偏见的提议。本研究为人类对通用语言理解的正式定量研究做出了贡献。（PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA，保留所有权利）
